question: When did the first nationalisation of banks take place in India?
solution:
The correct answer is 1__**949**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **first nationalization of banks** in India took place in **1949** when the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** was nationalized. 
 
• The RBI was made the central bank of the country, taking over the responsibility for regulating and controlling the monetary system, which was previously under private ownership.
 
• However, the **major nationalization of commercial banks** occurred later, in **1969**, when the Government of India nationalized **14 major commercial banks** to increase control over the banking sector and to ensure that credit was provided to key sectors of the economy, such as agriculture and industry. 
 
• The aim was to direct the banks to contribute to the nation’s development and reduce dependence on foreign banks.
 
• So, while **1949** marks the nationalization of the RBI, **1969** is often cited as the year of the first significant nationalization of commercial banks.
